en: The Sūtra on the Wish-Fulfilling Maṇi Dhāraṇī Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Court Dispersing Grandee, Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial,
and Great Master of the Transmission of the Dharma, the Subject Shi Hu, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying in the city of Kāliṅga in the kingdom of Śrāvastī.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Venerable Ānanda.
Now there is a dhāraṇī that can eliminate all violent and malevolent thunderbolts;
you should receive and uphold this *Sūtra of the Wish-Fulfilling Jewel of the Parittā*.
This was personally proclaimed by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past;
I now proclaim it as well,
out of great compassion for this world.
"It brings benefit, peace, and happiness to all sentient beings in the heavens and among humans.
Ānanda replied, "So be it, World-Honored One;
I wish to hear it and shall now receive and uphold it."
The Buddha told Ānanda,
"You should know that in the eastern direction there is a thunderbolt named Agga;
in the southern direction there is a thunderbolt named Setthilu."
In the western direction there is a thunderbolt named Cāṣa;
in the northern direction there is a thunderbolt named Svanamānī.
Ānanda, if there are sons or daughters of good family...
If one knows the names and the locations and directions of these thunderbolts,
no thunderbolt will frighten that person. Furthermore,
wherever one writes down these names of the thunderbolts, [no harm shall come].
By upholding and making offerings [to this],
one cannot be harmed by any lightning or thunderbolts.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these words of the protective mantra-verse:
*Tadyathā | nime nime nime dhare tare luke lukini śūrabhāṇi nirakṣame sarvavinyūpāye vyāhe svāhā.* At that time, the Noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara was present within the great assembly.
Immediately rising from his seat, he joined his palms toward the Buddha and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, regarding this True Dharma..."
It also sets forth the mantra syllables for protection: *tadyathā* | *viṃśapratyātmake pratya-mi-tri-ṣṭe mukte* || 2 ||
Samayaprabhāsakarī anantari pannari śviti pannarava-sinmate karakāvera-biṅgala-kiṣṇadhi.
MUKṢI RA-KṢI RA-KṢI-M Ā SARVA-KĀRA-MŪRTI-YOGBHAGE MA ME PAŚYANTU SARVA-KĀ...
*Āvāhayārya-vajragīti-śvara-teja-sasvāhā.* At that time, the Lord of Secrets, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi...
He approached the Buddha, joined his palms in prostration,
and addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
within this True Dharma, I now..."
He also spoke these dharani-mantra verses:
*Tadyathā | muñce muñce muñce mate mate sumate mahāmate hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ mātṛliṇasiddhe prabandhavajrapratiṣṭha svāhā*. "O Bhagavat, this dharani of mine..."
It is named "The Invincible One Who Protects Sentient Beings.
If anyone writes it down or recollects it,
they shall be completely liberated from all terrors and untimely deaths.
At that time, Mahābrahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World,
addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
for the benefit of all sentient beings,"
Within this True Dharma, there are also spoken dhāraṇī mantra syllables:
*tadyathā* | *hile mile jile svāhā* | *brahmabhumahābrahmanibrahmagrahipuṣṭaśāstari svāhā*. "World-Honored One, this dhāraṇī of mine is named the Brahmā Staff."
It protects all sentient beings,
keeps them far from untimely death, prevents the arising of fear, and is able to extinguish all sinful karma.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas...
He approached the Buddha, stood before him with palms joined in homage, prostrated at his feet,
and addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
regarding this True Dharma..."
He also spoke these dhāraṇī mantra syllables:

*tadyathā | buddhamādanīmaninikauri-ghaṇṭari-jaṇḍale-maṇḍe-pukvasi-sasara-pratīhīna-madhyuṇḍa-dhāraṇī-mandurī-nike-cakrāvakiśavariśavari svāhā*. "World-Honored One, this dhāraṇī of mine is named 'Vajrāsana' (The Diamond Throne)."
They shall be liberated from all fears and remain far removed from all premature death.
At that time, the Heavenly Kings Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Virūḍhaka, Virūpākṣa, and Vaiśravaṇa together approached the Buddha, joined their palms, and prostrated at his feet.
They addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, regarding this True Dharma,
we shall also proclaim dharani mantras and verses."

*Tadyathā | puṣpe supuṣpe | dūbe pārihārī | arye prajñaptite | śānte nirmukte | maṅgale he rājan āgaccha sādhu vidi svāhā.* "World-Honored One, we, the Four Great Heavenly Kings, have composed this dhāraṇī called 'Fearlessness'."
He bestows fearlessness upon those who are terrified;
he causes those who face untimely death to be spared and their lifespans extended.
At that time, there was also a great ocean dragon king.
The nāga kings Mahāmati, Vidyutprabha, Anavatapta, Vidyunjihva, and Śataprabha all went to where the Buddha was,
joined their palms, prostrated at his feet, and addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One..."
I possess a dhāraṇī named "Wish-Fulfilling Jewel" which protects sentient beings.
If anyone writes it down or recites it, [they shall be protected].
It can eliminate all fears of thunder and lightning,
all premature deaths, all poisons, and all malignant diseases; furthermore,
inauspicious spirits and deities shall find no opportunity to cause harm.
"Bhagavān, if one maintains this mantra, we nāgas will all feel compassion and not give rise to jealousy.
What do you think? How could those belonging to the nāga realm harbor a mind of jealousy?"
If one hears this Dharma without envy,
the dhāraṇī is as follows: Tadyathā | Añjali | Māmali | Amṛte |...
The Emperor [recited]: *akṣaye avyaye punye pariyaye sarvabhāva-praśamani svāhā aryaputra-saubhāgya*.
*Īṃ kīye svāhā; indraśānaye svāhā; mīṅgaśānaye svāhā.* At that time, the World-Honored One heard those words from Mahābrahmā, Śakra Devendra, and the four world-protecting kings.
The Great Dragon Kings and others spoke this dhāraṇī, praising it, saying: "Excellent, excellent!
It enables many people to attain the great medicine of peace."
"You all must protect, uphold, and propagate the True Dharma.
After the Buddha had spoken this sutra,
the entire assembly— including devas, nāgas, asuras, gandharvas, and others— [rejoiced].
All were greatly rejoiced, believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
Thus ends the *Buddha-spoken Sūtra of the Wish-Fulfilling Maṇi Dhāraṇī*.
